title: Persistent TCP connection scale-out recovery at 20,000 subscriptions
research_question: After Kubernetes scales the subscriber service from one Pod to four Pods, does guarded DQL probe promotion and persistent-connection migration drain a fixed backlog faster than Kubernetes scale-out alone, when all pre-existing TCP connections remain pinned to the original Pod?

mechanism_under_test.pre_scale_topology: one subscriber Pod with ten established persistent connections
mechanism_under_test.post_scale_topology: four available subscriber Pods; the ten established connections remain pinned to Pod 0
mechanism_under_test.dql_path: sample a subscription-free probe through the load balancer, select only admissible actions, promote a useful probe, migrate the complete subscription set from one source connection, retire the source, and create a replacement probe
mechanism_under_test.baseline_path: add Pods but retain all ten established persistent connections and subscriptions on Pod 0
mechanism_under_test.isolation_rule: subscriptions and backlog start evenly distributed across the ten connections, so connection-count and connection-backlog rebalancing are not initial explanations for the result

primary_comparison.decision_rule: The paired bootstrap 95% confidence interval for DQL minus baseline backlog AUC has an upper bound below zero and the one-sided paired sign-randomization p-value is below 0.05.

validity_checks: ten active persistent connections initially terminate on Pod 0
four subscriber Pods are available after scale-out
each connection initially carries 2,000 subscriptions and 77,500,000 queued events
a probe on an idle scaled-out Pod makes migration admissible
the scale-out-only baseline performs no migration
